+  # error-set #2 (return type) helpers: an optional constant-integer value, an optional

   def num_mix_tail(Tail, Dict(String, String), Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) Bool
   def num_mix_tail(TClose, _, _) := false
   def num_mix_tail(TCons(e), env, ic) := num_mix(e, env, ic)
+
+  # ── error set #2: return-type mismatch (ADR-0064/0034) — the canonical type error ──
+  # Rian.Check.check_return: a clause body whose inferred type contradicts the declared
+  # return is REJECTED. `ret_bad` returns true iff the body is a PROVABLE mismatch, in the
+  # same three-way order as the reference: a GENERIC return (mentions a `forall` tvar) is
+  # skipped; a constant-of-literals body that ADOPTS the declared width must FIT its range
+  # (out-of-range is bad); otherwise the inferred body type must be ASSIGNABLE (directional
+  # widening) to the return. CONSERVATIVE: an `unknown` body is assignable to anything (so
+  # it never rejects), and an `Fn(...)` return is skipped (this `unify` has no Fn-structural
+  # rule — a documented tail rather than a false reject).
+  pub def ret_bad(body Core, ret String, env Dict(String, String), ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) Bool
+  pub def ret_bad(body, ret, env, ic)
+    if has_tvar(ret) do
+      false
+    else
+      ret_bad_concrete(body, ret, env, ic)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def ret_bad_concrete(body Core, ret String, env Dict(String, String), ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) Bool
+  def ret_bad_concrete(body, ret, env, ic)
+    if lit_adopts(body, ret) do
+      lit_range_bad(body, ret)
+    else
+      assignable(infer_ic(body, env, ic), ret) == false
+    end
+  end
+
+  # `from` is assignable to `to` (Rian.Check.assignable?): identical, either unknown, or an
+  # `Fn(...)` on either side (skipped, see above); else for two numerics a lossless WIDENING;
+  # else exact unification must not mismatch.
+  def assignable(from String, to String) Bool
+  def assignable(from, to)
+    if from == to or from == "unknown" or to == "unknown" or is_fn(from) or is_fn(to) do
+      true
+    else
+      assignable_num(num_kind(from), num_kind(to), from, to)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def assignable_num(NumKind, NumKind, String, String) Bool
+  def assignable_num(Nk(fk, fw), Nk(tk, tw), _, _) := num_widens(Nk(fk, fw), Nk(tk, tw))
+  def assignable_num(_, _, from, to) := unify(from, to) != "mismatch"
+
+  # the lossless numeric widening lattice (Rian.Check.num_widens?): `from ⊑ to`. Same-kind
+  # int/uint/float widen to an equal-or-wider width; `uint ⊑ int` needs a strictly wider
+  # signed width; `int/uint ⊑ float` only when exactly representable in the mantissa.
+  def num_widens(NumKind, NumKind) Bool
+  def num_widens(Nk(fk, fa), Nk(tk, tb)) := widen(fk, fa, tk, tb)
+  def num_widens(_, _) := false
+
+  def widen(String, Int53, String, Int53) Bool
+  def widen("int", a, "int", b) := a <= b
+  def widen("uint", a, "uint", b) := a <= b
+  def widen("uint", a, "int", b) := a < b
+  def widen("int", a, "float", b) := a - 1 <= mantissa(b)
+  def widen("uint", a, "float", b) := a <= mantissa(b)
+  def widen("float", a, "float", b) := a <= b
+  def widen(_, _, _, _) := false
+
+  def mantissa(Int53) Int53
+  def mantissa(64) := 53
+  def mantissa(32) := 24
+  def mantissa(_) := 0
+
+  # Rian.Check.body_literal_adopts?: a constant-of-literals body adopts the declared width
+  # — an INTEGER literal adopts any `Int*`/`UInt*`, a FLOAT literal any `Float*` (cross-kind
+  # does NOT adopt). Recurses through arithmetic, `if`/`case` branches, single-expr blocks,
+  # and a closed list literal into `Vec(ElemT)`.
+  def lit_adopts(Core, String) Bool
+  def lit_adopts(CNum(t), ret) := lit_scalar_adopts(t, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(CUnary("-", a), ret) := lit_adopts(a, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(CBin(op, l, r), ret) := arith_op(op) and lit_adopts(l, ret) and lit_adopts(r, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(CIf(_, t, e), ret) := lit_adopts(t, ret) and lit_adopts(e, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(CCase(_, arms), ret) := arms_adopt(arms, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(CBlock([SExpr(e)]), ret) := lit_adopts(e, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(CList(elems, TClose), ret) := list_adopts(elems, ret)
+  def lit_adopts(_, _) := false
+
+  def lit_scalar_adopts(t String, ret String) Bool := if int_literal(t) do int_type(ret) else float_type(ret) end
+
+  def arms_adopt(Vec(Arm), String) Bool
+  def arms_adopt([], _) := false
+  def arms_adopt([CArm(_, b) | rest], ret) := lit_adopts(b, ret) and rest_arms_adopt(rest, ret)
+
+  def rest_arms_adopt(Vec(Arm), String) Bool
+  def rest_arms_adopt([], _) := true
+  def rest_arms_adopt([CArm(_, b) | rest], ret) := lit_adopts(b, ret) and rest_arms_adopt(rest, ret)
+
+  def list_adopts(elems Vec(Core), ret String) Bool := list_adopts_v(elems, vec_elem_opt(ret))
+
+  def list_adopts_v(Vec(Core), VecOpt) Bool
+  def list_adopts_v(_, VNone) := false
+  def list_adopts_v([], VSome(_)) := true
+  def list_adopts_v([e | rest], VSome(et)) := lit_adopts(e, et) and list_adopts_v(rest, VSome(et))
+
+  def float_type(t String) Bool := float_word(Prim.str_chars(t))
+
+  def float_word(Vec(Int53)) Bool
+  def float_word(['F', 'l', 'o', 'a', 't' | rest]) := all_digits(rest)
+  def float_word(_) := false
+
+  # Rian.Check.lit_range_error/oor_scan: a constant integer in the (literal) body that falls
+  # outside the declared fixed-width range is bad. A `Vec(ElemT)` checks each element vs
+  # `ElemT`; the `>Int53` widths (Int64/Int128/UInt64/UInt128) have no port range check yet
+  # (`BNone`, a documented tail — their bounds would be bignums).
+  def lit_range_bad(body Core, ret String) Bool
+  def lit_range_bad(body, ret)
+    case vec_elem_opt(ret) do
+      VSome(et) -> lrb_list(list_elems(body), et)
+      VNone -> lrb_scalar(body, ret)
+    end
+  end
+
+  def lrb_list(Vec(Core), String) Bool
+  def lrb_list([], _) := false
+  def lrb_list([e | rest], et) := lit_range_bad(e, et) or lrb_list(rest, et)
+
+  def lrb_scalar(body Core, ret String) Bool := lrb_bounds(body, width_bounds(ret))
+
+  def lrb_bounds(Core, BoundOpt) Bool
+  def lrb_bounds(_, BNone) := false
+  def lrb_bounds(body, B(lo, hi)) := oor_scan(body, lo, hi)
+
+  def oor_scan(Core, Int53, Int53) Bool
+  def oor_scan(CIf(_, t, e), lo, hi) := oor_scan(t, lo, hi) or oor_scan(e, lo, hi)
+  def oor_scan(CCase(_, arms), lo, hi) := oor_arms(arms, lo, hi)
+  def oor_scan(CBlock([SExpr(e)]), lo, hi) := oor_scan(e, lo, hi)
+  def oor_scan(e, lo, hi) := oor_leaf(const_int_opt(e), lo, hi)
+
+  def oor_arms(Vec(Arm), Int53, Int53) Bool
+  def oor_arms([], _, _) := false
+  def oor_arms([CArm(_, b) | rest], lo, hi) := oor_scan(b, lo, hi) or oor_arms(rest, lo, hi)
+
+  def oor_leaf(IntOpt, Int53, Int53) Bool
+  def oor_leaf(ISome(v), lo, hi) := v < lo or v > hi
+  def oor_leaf(INone, _, _) := false
+
+  def const_int_opt(Core) IntOpt
+  def const_int_opt(CNum(t)) := if int_literal(t) do ISome(int_value(t)) else INone end
+  def const_int_opt(CUnary("-", a)) := neg_int(const_int_opt(a))
+  def const_int_opt(_) := INone
+
+  def neg_int(IntOpt) IntOpt
+  def neg_int(ISome(v)) := ISome(0 - v)
+  def neg_int(INone) := INone
+
+  def int_value(t String) Int53 := parse_digits(only_digits(Prim.str_chars(t)), 0)
+
+  def only_digits(Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53)
+  def only_digits([]) := []
+  def only_digits([c | rest]) := if c >= 48 and c <= 57 do [c | only_digits(rest)] else only_digits(rest) end
+
+  def list_elems(Core) Vec(Core)
+  def list_elems(CList(elems, _)) := elems
+  def list_elems(CBlock([SExpr(e)])) := list_elems(e)
+  def list_elems(_) := []
+
+  def vec_elem_opt(ret String) VecOpt := vopt(parse_parametric(ret))
+
+  def vopt(PpRes) VecOpt
+  def vopt(Pp(name, args)) := if name == "Vec" do vfirst(args) else VNone end
+  def vopt(PpNone) := VNone
+
+  def vfirst(Vec(String)) VecOpt
+  def vfirst([]) := VNone
+  def vfirst([x | _]) := VSome(x)
+
+  def width_bounds(String) BoundOpt
+  def width_bounds("Int8") := B(0 - 128, 127)
+  def width_bounds("Int16") := B(0 - 32768, 32767)
+  def width_bounds("Int32") := B(0 - 2147483648, 2147483647)
+  def width_bounds("Int53") := B(0 - 9007199254740991, 9007199254740991)
+  def width_bounds("UInt8") := B(0, 255)
+  def width_bounds("UInt16") := B(0, 65535)
+  def width_bounds("UInt32") := B(0, 4294967295)
+  def width_bounds(_) := BNone
 end

+  # ── self-CHECKING gate: return-type mismatch (ADR-0064/0034, P3) ───────────────────
+  # The FOURTH build-loop gate — the canonical type error — reusing the equivalence-locked
+  # `Checker.ret_bad` (checker.rian, locked by checker_rettype_fixpoint_test): a `d_func`
+  # whose body's inferred type contradicts its declared return (tuple position 5) is
+  # REFUSED with `{:type_error, name}`. Same `d_func` scoping + collapsing-projection tail
+  # as the numeric-mix gate — an `if`/`case`/block-BODIED return infers `unknown` under the
+  # collapse and is conservatively skipped (never a false reject, so v1==v2 is unaffected).
+  def first_ret_error(decls Vec(Tuple)) String
+  def first_ret_error([]) := ""
+  def first_ret_error([{:d_func, _, name, params, ret, _, body} | rest])
+    if func_ret_bad(params, ret, body) do
+      name
+    else
+      first_ret_error(rest)
+    end
+  end
+  def first_ret_error([{:d_mod, _, inner} | rest]) := mod_ret(first_ret_error(inner), rest)
+  def first_ret_error([_ | rest]) := first_ret_error(rest)
+
+  def mod_ret(inner String, rest Vec(Tuple)) String
+    if inner == "" do
+      first_ret_error(rest)
+    else
+      inner
+    end
+  end
+
+  # unlike num_mix (which WALKS the body for a mix anywhere), the return gate needs the
+  # body's VALUE type — its result expression. We project the lowered block's last
+  # expression (the common `def f(…) T := expr` is a one-statement block) and hand THAT to
+  # `Checker.ret_bad`. A multi-statement block whose result depends on a local bind infers
+  # `unknown` (the local isn't in the param env) → conservatively skipped — a documented tail.
+  def func_ret_bad(params Vec(Tuple), ret String, body Tuple) Bool
+    tenv := param_tenv(params)
+    Checker.ret_bad(to_chk(block_result(lower_body(desugar_interp(tenv, body)))), ret, tenv_dict(tenv), Prim.map_new())
+  end
+
+  def block_result(Block) Core
+  def block_result(Block(stmts)) := last_expr(stmts)
+
+  def last_expr(Vec(Stmt)) Core
+  def last_expr([]) := CId("")
+  def last_expr([SExpr(e)]) := e
+  def last_expr([SBind(_, e)]) := e
+  def last_expr([STypedBind(_, _, e)]) := e

+
+  # an UNTYPED param carries type "" — omit it so the checker infers `unknown` for it

   def tenv_dict([]) := Prim.map_new()

   def tenv_dict([{n, t} | rest]) := Prim.map_put(tenv_dict(rest), n, t)

+defmodule Rian.CheckerRetTypeFixpointTest do
+  # async: false — loads compiler/checker.rian into the VM via :code.load_binary.
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: false
+
+  alias Rian.{Beam, Core, Check, Pratt}
+
+  # Self-hosting fixpoint (ADR-0063) for the type checker's SECOND ERROR SET — the
+  # canonical type error, RETURN-TYPE mismatch (Rian.Check.check_return, ADR-0064/0034).
+  # `compiler/checker.rian`'s `ret_bad/4` returns `true` iff a clause body's inferred type
+  # provably contradicts the declared return: a generic return is skipped; a
+  # constant-of-literals body that ADOPTS the declared width must FIT its range; otherwise
+  # the inferred body type must be ASSIGNABLE (directional widening) to the return.
+  #
+  # LOCK: for each corpus function the port's `ret_bad` (over the body's FAITHFUL Core, the
+  # clause's param env, an empty `ic`) must AGREE with whether the REAL `Rian.Check.check/1`
+  # reports the return-type error. `check_return` runs before binds/bounds/numeric-mix in
+  # the gate chain, so a return mismatch is the message that fires. The corpus uses
+  # param/literal operands so the empty `ic` is irrelevant. Because the inference is itself
+  # already equivalence-locked (checker_infer_fixpoint_test), agreeing body types compose
+  # into an agreeing return decision.
+
+  setup_all do
+    {:ok, mod} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/checker.rian"), :rian_checker_rettype_fixpoint)
+    {:ok, mod: mod}
+  end
+
+  # {label, body expression, param env, declared return, full function (for the reference)}.
+  # NEGATIVE = a provable return mismatch → BOTH the port and Rian.Check must flag it.
+  @negative [
+    {"Int64 ⋢ Float64", "a", %{"a" => "Int64"}, "Float64", "def f(a Int64) Float64 := a"},
+    {"String ⋢ Int64", ~S|"hi"|, %{}, "Int64", ~S|def f() Int64 := "hi"|},
+    {"narrowing Int16→Int8", "a", %{"a" => "Int16"}, "Int8", "def f(a Int16) Int8 := a"},
+    {"Bool ⋢ Int64", "b", %{"b" => "Bool"}, "Int64", "def f(b Bool) Int64 := b"},
+    {"literal out of range", "9999", %{}, "Int8", "def f() Int8 := 9999"},
+    {"neg literal out of range", "-200", %{}, "Int8", "def f() Int8 := -200"},
+    {"Vec elem out of range", "[1, 2, 9999]", %{}, "Vec(Int8)",
+     "def f() Vec(Int8) := [1, 2, 9999]"}
+  ]
+
+  # POSITIVE = NO mismatch → BOTH must pass. Widening, literal adoption in range, identity,
+  # int-literal→float, conservative unknown, and a generic return.
+  @positive [
+    {"Int32 ⊑ Float64", "a", %{"a" => "Int32"}, "Float64", "def f(a Int32) Float64 := a"},
+    {"Int8 := 5 (adopts, in range)", "5", %{}, "Int8", "def f() Int8 := 5"},
+    {"Int64 identity", "a", %{"a" => "Int64"}, "Int64", "def f(a Int64) Int64 := a"},
+    {"int-lit ⊑ Float64", "66", %{}, "Float64", "def f() Float64 := 66"},
+    {"Vec elems in range", "[1, 2, 3]", %{}, "Vec(Int8)", "def f() Vec(Int8) := [1, 2, 3]"},
+    {"untyped param → unknown", "a", %{}, "Int64", "def f(a, b) Int64 := a"},
+    {"generic return (skipped)", "x", %{"x" => "T"}, "T", "def id(x T) T forall T := x"}
+  ]
+
+  defp inj(%Core.ENum{text: t}), do: {:c_num, t}
+  defp inj(%Core.EStr{value: v}), do: {:c_str, v}
+  defp inj(%Core.EChar{value: c}), do: {:c_char, c}
+  defp inj(%Core.EId{name: n}), do: {:c_id, n}
+  defp inj(%Core.EUnary{op: op, arg: a}), do: {:c_unary, op, inj(a)}
+  defp inj(%Core.EBin{op: op, left: l, right: r}), do: {:c_bin, op, inj(l), inj(r)}
+  defp inj(%Core.ECall{fun: %Core.EId{name: f}, args: as}), do: {:c_call, f, Enum.map(as, &inj/1)}
+  defp inj(%Core.EIf{cond: c, then: t, else: e}), do: {:c_if, inj(c), inj(t), inj(e)}
+  defp inj(%Core.EBlock{stmts: stmts}), do: {:c_block, Enum.map(stmts, &inj_stmt/1)}
+  defp inj(%Core.ECase{scrut: s, arms: arms}), do: {:c_case, inj(s), Enum.map(arms, &inj_arm/1)}
+
+  defp inj(%Core.EList{elems: elems, tail: tail}),
+    do: {:c_list, Enum.map(elems, &inj/1), inj_tail(tail)}
+
+  defp inj(%Core.ELambda{params: ps, body: body}),
+    do: {:c_lambda, Enum.map(ps, &inj_param/1), inj(body)}
+
+  defp inj_tail(nil), do: :t_close
+  defp inj_tail(:close), do: :t_close
+  defp inj_tail(tail), do: {:t_cons, inj(tail)}
+  defp inj_param({n, nil}), do: {:lp, n, :pt_none}
+  defp inj_param({n, t}), do: {:lp, n, {:pt_some, t}}
+  defp inj_stmt({:expr, e}), do: {:s_expr, inj(e)}
+  defp inj_stmt({:bind, n, e}), do: {:s_bind, n, inj(e)}
+  defp inj_arm({pat, _guard, body}), do: {:c_arm, inj_pat(pat), inj(body)}
+  defp inj_pat(%Core.PVar{name: n}), do: {:p_var, n}
+  defp inj_pat(%Core.PCtor{ctor: c, args: args}), do: {:p_ctor, c, Enum.map(args, &inj_pat/1)}
+  defp inj_pat(_), do: :p_other
+
+  defp port_ret(mod, body, env, ret),
+    do: mod.ret_bad(inj(Core.from_expr(Pratt.parse(body))), ret, env, %{})
+
+  # the reference's verdict isolated to the return-type gate by its message (the corpus is
+  # built so a return mismatch is the only error a function carries, and check_return runs
+  # before the binds/bounds/numeric-mix gates).
+  defp ref_ret(src) do
+    case Check.check(src) do
+      :ok ->
+        false
+
+      {:error, msg} ->
+        String.contains?(msg, "declared return type is") or
+          String.contains?(msg, "out of range for")
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "ret_bad agrees with Rian.Check.check_return (the lock)" do
+    test "every NEGATIVE case is flagged by BOTH the port and the reference", %{mod: mod} do
+      for {label, body, env, ret, src} <- @negative do
+        assert ref_ret(src),
+               "reference did not flag the return mismatch in #{label}: #{inspect(src)}"
+
+        assert port_ret(mod, body, env, ret),
+               "port ret_bad missed the mismatch in #{label}: #{inspect(body)} ⋢ #{ret}"
+      end
+    end
+
+    test "every POSITIVE case is passed by BOTH the port and the reference", %{mod: mod} do
+      for {label, body, env, ret, src} <- @positive do
+        refute ref_ret(src), "reference flagged a non-mismatch in #{label}: #{inspect(src)}"
+
+        refute port_ret(mod, body, env, ret),
+               "port ret_bad false-flagged #{label}: #{inspect(body)} : #{ret}"
+      end
+    end
+
+    test "port and reference agree on every corpus entry (the equivalence lock)", %{mod: mod} do
+      for {label, body, env, ret, src} <- @negative ++ @positive do
+        assert port_ret(mod, body, env, ret) == ref_ret(src),
+               "ret_bad DIVERGED from Rian.Check on #{label}: #{inspect(src)}"
+      end
+    end
+  end
+end

     end

+  describe "the return-type gate is WIRED into build — a return mismatch is REJECTED" do
